Mounts.description:
Storage mounts attached to a pod. `persistent` (the volume disk) is
mutually exclusive with both `network` and `global` (enforced at the
handler with 400 if combined). A pod takes up to 4 network volumes
and 1 global volume. Every network volume must be in the pod's data
center, each volume may be listed once, and mount paths must not
overlap; a request that breaks one of these is rejected. To change a
pod's mounts after creation, see `UpdatePodMounts`.

network.description: Up to 4 network volumes, all in the pod's data center.

global.description:
At most one global volume, on GPU and CPU pods, with no data
center constraint. Combinable with `network` but not with
`persistent` (rejected with 400): a persistent disk is dropped
whenever a volume is attached. Same PATCH rules as `network`.

GlobalMount.description:
Reference to a GlobalVolume. Usage-billed, so it has no size. On a
pod, the volume can be mounted, moved, or unmounted after creation
(see `UpdatePodMounts`).

path.description: Mount path inside the container. Optional; a default is chosen for you when omitted.

NetworkMount.description:
Reference to a NetworkVolume. Custom paths are honored at runtime on
both GPU and CPU pods. On a pod, the volume can be mounted, moved,
or unmounted after creation (see `UpdatePodMounts`).

volumeId.description: ID of an existing NetworkVolume in the same data center as the pod.

path.description: Mount path inside the container. No default — must be specified explicitly.

PersistentMount.description:
Host-local persistent storage. Pinned to the pod's host machine — data
does not survive a host failure. Disallowed on CPU pods. Mutually
exclusive with NetworkMount. Deprecated: prefer NetworkMount for any
data you cannot recreate.

size.description: Host-local persistent storage in GB. Minimum 10 GB.

path.description: Mount path inside the container. May be changed via PATCH.
